transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to discuss the first-year composition program's proposal to pilot an AI writing-feedback platform in two sections next term. As I understand it, the platform can generate comments on student drafts and can be configured for different levels of instructor control. Before I make a decision on whether this pilot may proceed, I want to make sure we've gone through our routine review process. I'd like to hear from both the writing program and the privacy office about any instructional or data-handling requirements we should be aware of. Could someone from each of those areas share their perspective?

transcript.text: I should share an important update before we go further. This week, I finalized the writing program's adopted pilot standard for AI writing-feedback platforms. The standard permits the platform only for formative feedback, requires an instructor to review every generated suggestion before it is released to a student, and prohibits using the platform to assign or determine grades. This standard has not yet been added to the proposal packet, so I want to make sure everyone here is aware of it now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Professor Ellis. I should also share the privacy office's findings. I've completed my vendor review of the proposed AI writing-feedback platform. The review found that approval requires institutional single sign-on and a signed addendum stating that the vendor retains no student prompts or submissions. The vendor has confirmed it will accept those terms. However, I should note that my review memo is still awaiting attachment to the proposal packet, so it hasn't formally been added yet.
